title: Epoch handshake & sharding coordination — architectural scrub
content:
Meeting: architectural scrub — epoch-based handshake and cooperative sharding
Date: 2025-02-12
Attendees: Priya (owner), Ethan, Sofia, Jasper, Ana, Sam (SRE), Lina (platform) dropped in for 20m
Location: zoom / #infra-arch Slack thread (see thread ts: 2025-02-10 16:03)
Purpose: review RFC draft for using epoch-handshakes to coordinate shard rebalancing and eviction smoothing across serving fleet. Goal was to converge on a default approach for Dedicated + Hosted that minimizes tail-latency spikes during rebalances and reduces cross-tenant noisy neighbor effects.

Context / Why this matters:
- current reactive sharding (slot-level preemption) causes short tail spikes when many sessions migrate concurrently (observed in 2024-11 stress test).
- customers with reserved capacity see variability; we need a predictable, staged handoff protocol to avoid cascading KV cache invalidations.
- previous experiments (linked PR #879) showed good throughput but interaction with prefix caching not fully tested.

Quick background (short):
- epoch = lightweight monotonic counter per allocation/pool used during planned adjustments
- handshake = multi-step acknowledgement among source slot, target slot, and model-hotstore controller to ensure KV cache warm-up before traffic cutover
- objective: reduce request retries + model kernel cold starts + prefix cache churn during moves

Proposals reviewed (high-level):
A) Conservative staged handshake (3-phase)
  - Phase 1: announce intent (epoch++) to candidate targets, prefetch warmup async
  - Phase 2: warm traffic mirrored (low-sample) for verification, targets report readiness metrics
  - Phase 3: cutover after quorum ok, source drains gracefully
  - Pros: safest for tail-latency; deterministic rollback points
  - Cons: higher coordination cost and transient duplicate model memory use; more network chatter

B) Opportunistic optimistic cutover
  - single-phase: mark target active, route fraction immediately, trust caching heuristics to warm quickly
  - Pros: low coord overhead, fast moves, good for benign loads
  - Cons: risk of spikes under high concurrency; harder to reason about regressions

C) Hybrid epoch-with-credit-smoothing (recommended direction to prototype)
  - use epoch to tag migrations but rely on slot-crediting window to ramp traffic smoothly (credit window size configurable per pool)
  - warmup tasks queued with prioritized prefetch (small sample sync mirroring) and KV-prefetch budget assigned by policy
  - fall back to staged handshake if health signals cross thresholds (latency or cache-miss rate)
  - Pros: balances safety and speed, incremental rollout path, aligns with Optimize recommendations (auto-batching + prefetch)
  - Cons: more moving parts; needs new observability hooks (per-epoch readiness and per-prefetch success rate)

Key tradeoffs discussed:
- Observability: must add epoch telemetry (per-epoch id, start/end times, readiness signals) to trace spans; otherwise diagnosing regressions will be painful. Jasper insisted that sampling rate should be low-by-default to avoid cost. Action item below.
- Backpressure interaction: Sam emphasized how this interacts with existing resource-crediting and preemption. If we ramp too fast we can cause local queuing inside the runtime even if target reports 'ready'. Need a safety valve to clamp incoming rate (leaky-bucket per-epoch).
- KV cache warming: Sofia showed microbench sim where warmup reduces token cost by ~18% after 3s warm window for typical convo prefixes. But if >20 sessions move same model shard concurrently, perf benefit disappears. So coordination across pool matters.

Decisions / Consensus (informal):
- Prototype path: implement C (Hybrid epoch-with-credit-smoothing) in runtime branch + platform feature flag. We will default to staged-handshake only for enterprise private deployments with strict SLAs (configurable) — but C is default for Hosted to optimize speed.
- Minimum viable telemetry: epoch_id, epoch_start_ts, target_ready_ts, warm_prefetch_success (0/1), cutover_ts, cutover_latency_p50/p95 sampled. Add a lightweight per-epoch health event emitted to event bus.
- Safety thresholds (initial): p95 latency increase > 15% or kv-miss rate increase > 25% during warm window triggers automatic rollback and revert to staged handshake for next epoch. Lina to codify thresholds in policy config.

Open concerns (parking lot):
- Cross-pool coordinated moves: if we rebalance many tenants at once across racks, how to avoid network saturation? Need to add jitter/coordinator backoff. (Open: INF-2399)
- Multi-variant models: migrating variant A vs variant B may have different warm profiles. Should epoch be variant-aware? (Discussed: yes, tag epoch with variant metadata.)
- Rollback complexity: who owns the rollback? The platform controller will perform rollback automatically, but SRE must be alerted. Ensure alerts are not noisy.

Sim numbers / quick bench notes (from Sofia):
- single slot move (1 session): median warm time 1.8s, p95 3.5s; KV cache hit rate after warm ~78% vs 52% cold
- 10 concurrent moves in same pool: median warm 2.1s, p95 6.2s; hit rate drops to ~55%
- backpressure clamp at 50 rps per-epoch kept queue lengths stable in 99% sim runs; at 100 rps we saw queue growth for small GPUs

Action items (owners & tickets):
- Lina: write platform policy draft for safety thresholds + feature flag gating (ticket JIRA-INF-2402). Due: 2025-02-20.
- Jasper: add epoch telemetry proto + sampling strategy; open PR to runtime repo (PR WIP, see linked PR #879). Due: 2025-02-18.
- Sofia: extended sim across mixed-variant workloads and produce CSV of results; include cold-start interactions with prefix cache. (JIRA-INF-2405). Due: 2025-02-22.
- Ethan: prototype credit-smoothing window and leaky-bucket clamp in slot allocator; bench locally and report. (GH-branch: epoch-credits-smoothed). Due: 2025-02-19.
- Priya (me): collate notes + produce trimmed RFC v0.2 incorporating decisions and add rollback playbook. Post to Confluence; link in JIRA-INF-2345. Due: 2025-02-16.
- Sam (SRE): draft alerting runbook for rollback events to avoid alert storms. (JIRA-INF-2408). Due: 2025-02-21.

Next meetings / follow-ups:
- Quick sync: 2025-02-18 (30m) to review PRs and telemetry plan (invite list: eng-runtime, platform, SRE).
- Dry run: schedule small rolling migration test in staging (target window 2025-02-24) to validate thresholds.

Notes to self / rough thoughts (informal):
- consider using existing prefix caching prefetch hooks rather than new heavy machinery — keep API minimal.
- if we tag epoch with sampling key we can reuse existing tracing infra to stitch events back to a session id (cheap).
- Ops concern: need clear visibility in Console for tenants experiencing frequent rebalances — add per-tenant rebalance metric.

Decisions summary (one-liner): prototype hybrid epoch + credit smoothing with clear rollback thresholds and minimal telemetry; staged handshake remains the safety net for stricter deployments.

Revision history:
- 2025-02-12: initial scrub notes (this doc)
- 2025-02-14: added sim numbers from Sofia and clarified action owners

References / links (quick):
- runtime PR wip: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/879
- RFC draft: confluence/RFC-epoch-handshake (internal)
- Jira tickets: JIRA-INF-2345 (RFC tracking), JIRA-INF-2399 (cross-pool), JIRA-INF-2402 (policy), JIRA-INF-2405 (sim), JIRA-INF-2408 (alerts)

End of notes.

-- Priya
